title: Camera distance bench: a real face photo, rescaled to simulate distance, through the real MediaPipe pipeline in Chrome
label: Measured (bench). Not a physical ruler test on devices.

method.face: MediaPipe test portrait (https://storage.googleapis.com/mediapipe-assets/portrait.jpg), drawn at scale s about the face centre on a 640×480 frame with a mid-grey background; one frame per video, looped by Chrome
method.physics: Pinhole camera: moving a face from d to d/s scales its image by s, so scale s is the face at (reference distance × S_REF ÷ s).
method.pipeline: lab.html from a production build (vite preview, no brotli step), shipped src/camera/distance.ts unchanged: MediaPipe Face Landmarker, irisWidthNorm()
method.calibration: k = 300 mm × median iris width at the reference scale (S_REF = 1.0257), as the app does at 30 cm
method.rawPrecision: Full-precision iris widths, captured by wrapping Number.prototype.toFixed in the page (lab.ts calls irisNorm.toFixed(5) once per frame); the app itself is unchanged

machine.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Laptop GPU, Intel(R) Arc(TM) Graphics
machine.webgl: Google Inc. (Intel) | ANGLE (Intel, Intel(R) Arc(TM) Graphics (0x00007D55) Direct3D11 vs_5_0 ps_5_0, D3D11)
machine.browser: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/153.0.0.0 Safari/537.36

delegate.note: MediaPipe created a WebGL 2 context ("GL version: 3.0 (OpenGL ES 3.0 (WebGL 2.0…") on the GPU listed under machine.webgl, so the app's first choice, the GPU delegate, loaded without falling back to CPU. MediaPipe also logged "Created TensorFlow Lite XNNPACK delegate for CPU" (it does this for a CPU-side helper graph); which sub-model runs where is not exposed.

limitations: One face (a single public test photo), frontal, evenly lit, perfectly still. Real use adds head movement, turning, glasses, poor light and different faces.
A flat photo is rescaled, so only image size changes with "distance"; real perspective changes of a 3D head are not reproduced. For the near-flat iris this is a small effect.
Above the photo's native size (simulated distances under about 31 cm) the image is upsampled, so it has less fine detail than a real close-up camera image.
This tests the pipeline's linearity and noise, not absolute accuracy: the uncalibrated (70° field-of-view) distance cannot be checked here because a photo has no true distance.

Frame rate: one Windows laptop (see machine). The 30 fps fake camera caps the normal runs; a 60 fps feed shows the headroom. Phones will be slower. 3 of 30 runs had brief dips (lowest 1-second reading 8 fps) while other jobs were running on the laptop.

Physical accuracy of iris-based distance was evaluated by Google: 4.3% mean relative error (SD 2.4%) against an iPhone 11 depth sensor, over 200+ participants (https://research.google/blog/mediapipe-iris-real-time-iris-tracking-depth-estimation/). That is a separate, published result, not ours.
